subject.title: Cron Jobs Calendar View for Control UI

question: Should OpenClaw accept a repaired narrow 24-hour Cron Jobs timeline as the first Control UI slice, or require a broader daily/week calendar design before implementation?
rationale: The remaining work is a new Control UI product surface, the linked PR implements only part of the requested scope, and current main has since moved the Cron page architecture.

options.title: Repair Narrow Timeline First
options.body: Rebase and repair the linked PR or a replacement against the current Cron page, preserve current contracts, and treat day/week/drag-and-drop scope as follow-up product work.

options.title: Design Full Calendar Scope
options.body: Pause the linked implementation and define the daily, weekly, stats, details, and editing behavior before accepting implementation.

options.title: Decline Core Calendar View
options.body: Keep the current list/run-history UI as sufficient for core and close the issue plus linked implementation after a maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Repair Narrow Timeline First
recommendation.body: Rebase and repair the linked PR or a replacement against the current Cron page, preserve current contracts, and treat day/week/drag-and-drop scope as follow-up product work.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Cron page architecture now routes through the Control UI refactor this person authored, so they are the strongest code-history routing signal for the product-surface choice.
